parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a smooth, white-anodized aluminum rod with a matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing loop for attaching gear or ropes.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper can securely grasp the curved spine or the straight back section of the loop.
physics.reason: Carabiner bodies are typically forged or machined from solid metal stock to withstand high tensile loads, not hollow shells.

parts.description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a smooth, white-anodized aluminum rod with a matte finish.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing loop for attaching gear or ropes.

parts.name: nose lug

physics.Basic_description: A small protrusion at the tip of the carabiner body, matching the white anodized finish of the main loop.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the catch point where the gate wire latches to close the loop.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integral to the body to be grasped independently; gripper would contact the adjacent body loop.
physics.reason: Integral part of the solid forged or machined body structure.

parts.description: A small protrusion at the tip of the carabiner body, matching the white anodized finish of the main loop.
parts.function: Acts as the catch point where the gate wire latches to close the loop.

parts.name: wire loop

physics.Basic_description: A thin, bent metal wire forming the gate, appearing silver/grey against the white body in the RGB view.
physics.Functional_description: Springs open to allow attachment and snaps shut to secure the connection.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be pinched by fine-tipped grippers to manually open the gate, though fragile.
physics.reason: Wire gates are formed from solid round or oval cross-section steel wire.

parts.description: A thin, bent metal wire forming the gate, appearing silver/grey against the white body in the RGB view.
parts.function: Springs open to allow attachment and snaps shut to secure the connection.

parts.name: wire hinge plate

physics.Basic_description: A small structural component at the base of the gate, likely part of the body forging holding the hinge pin.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the hinge mechanism allowing the wire gate to pivot.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a viable grasp target due to small size and location near the hinge.
physics.reason: Part of the solid metal body structure surrounding the hinge.

parts.description: A small structural component at the base of the gate, likely part of the body forging holding the hinge pin.
parts.function: Houses the hinge mechanism allowing the wire gate to pivot.

parts.name: wire latch tip

physics.Basic_description: The very end of the wire gate where it contacts the nose lug.
physics.Functional_description: Interfaces with the nose lug to complete the closed loop.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp; interaction would be via the main wire loop.
physics.reason: End of the solid wire gate component.

parts.description: The very end of the wire gate where it contacts the nose lug.
parts.function: Interfaces with the nose lug to complete the closed loop.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A tiny cylindrical pin visible at the hinge joint, likely steel.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the axle for the wire gate to rotate around.
physics.Grasped_description: Impossible to grasp individually; embedded within the hinge assembly.
physics.reason: Pins are inherently solid cylindrical components.

parts.description: A tiny cylindrical pin visible at the hinge joint, likely steel.
parts.function: Acts as the axle for the wire gate to rotate around.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
